data.name: Title
data.value: Picture modes

data.name: Intro
data.value: Click a mode: brightness, blue light and color vibrance are set together. It does not touch the refresh rate, the calibration or the monitor's color preset.

data.name: Recommended
data.value: recommended

data.name: BestTitle
data.value: For the best picture (once)

data.name: BestStep1
data.value: 1. Monitor settings tab: Color preset Neutral (6500K, the most accurate built-in one); Custom RGB if you will run the setup wizard. Sharpness 4 (factory).

data.name: BestStep2
data.value: 2. Setup wizard: matches the white to the Pixel's screen and sets gamma 2.2 and grey balance by eye with patterns. This gives the most accurate color.

data.name: BestStep3
data.value: 3. Day mode for everyday use; Evening in the evening, Night in a dark room.

data.name: Purpose_Day
data.value: The most accurate picture for daytime and everyday work: no effects, 6500K white.

data.name: Purpose_Evening
data.value: Evening: warmer white (3400K), slightly lower brightness; less eye strain.

data.name: Purpose_Night
data.value: Dark room and before bed: very warm white (2700K), low brightness.

data.name: Purpose_Code
data.value: Long reading and code: slightly warm white (5000K); white pages don't glare.

data.name: Purpose_Film
data.value: Movies and video: more vivid colors (NVIDIA vibrance) to offset the TN panel's washed-out look; not accurate color.

data.name: Purpose_Game
data.value: Games: a little brighter and more vivid colors.

data.name: Purpose_DaVinci
data.value: DaVinci timeline: neutral, no effects; color decisions are made on the phone.
